title: X-ray machine-learning analysis reveals opposing Cd/Re displacements and Re 5d involvement in Cd₂Re₂O₇ structural order
summary: Unsupervised X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC) analyzed high-volume temperature-dependent diffraction data from Cd₂Re₂O₇. The extracted selection rules indicate that Cd and Re displacements are approximately equal in amplitude and opposite in phase, revealing a previously unrecognized involvement of Re 5d electrons in the structural order. The analysis also resolves X-ray diffraction evidence for fluctuations associated with the structural transitions. This is a data-driven interpretation of measured diffraction, not a new direct imaging of atom trajectories.
ai_technology: X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC), an interpretable unsupervised machine-learning method using Gaussian-mixture clustering and reciprocal-space label smoothing
organization: Cornell University; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Tennessee, Knoxville; University of Maryland; National Institute of Standards and Technology

evidence.tested: Unsupervised X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC) analyzed high-volume temperature-dependent diffraction data from Cd₂Re₂O₇.
evidence.unknown: The displacement relation and Re 5d involvement are physical interpretations inferred from XRD selection rules and X-TEC clustering, not direct atom-by-atom imaging. The work reports XRD evidence for a structural Goldstone mode; it does not claim that all Goldstone-mode physics in Cd₂Re₂O₇ was previously unknown. The findings concern the analyzed crystal and temperature-dependent synchrotron diffraction data.
evidence.ai_role: X-TEC clustered temperature trajectories of diffraction intensities across a high-volume reciprocal-space dataset to identify structural order parameters and weaker diffuse-scattering fluctuations. Its data-driven selection rules exposed the reciprocal-space pattern from which researchers inferred approximately equal, out-of-phase Cd and Re displacements and the Re 5d contribution; the manual crystallographic analysis would have required selecting only a small number of peaks.
